title: Boston or New York?
subtitle: Back from the holidays — comparatives: -er, more … than
canDo: I can compare two cities, people or things.
I can use -er, more … than and better / worse.
I can say which place I prefer and why.
teacherNotes: Türkçede "-den daha büyük", Arapçada "أكبر من" denir; İngilizcede sıra "bigger than". Tahtaya iki dilin sırasını alt alta yazmak işe yarar.
Tek heceli sıfatlarda son harf ikilenmesini (big → bigger, hot → hotter) tahtada renkli kalemle gösterin.
Konuşma: öğrenciler kendi şehirlerini başkentle veya Boston'la karşılaştırsın. "Which do you prefer?" sorusuyla bitirin.
Boston metrosu (1897) gerçekten ABD'nin en eski metrosu; New York'unki 1904'te açıldı. Öğrencilere küçük bir bilgi yarışması yapılabilir.

sections.title: Read
sections.heading: Two cities, one week
sections.intro: Elif's article for the school newsletter.
paragraphs: New York is only four hours from Boston by car, but the two cities are very different. Here are my notes from one week in the Big Apple.
First, New York is much bigger. More than eight million people live there. Boston has about 650,000 people, so New York is about twelve times bigger!
The buildings are taller, the streets are busier, and everybody walks faster.
Did you know that Boston's subway is older than New York's? It opened in 1897, seven years before the New York subway.
But the New York subway is bigger, and it runs all night. In Boston, the last train leaves after midnight.
New York is more expensive too. A coffee in Manhattan was four dollars. At Sam's café, it's only $2.50, and the cookies are better.
The pizza is cheaper in New York, though. Lucas ate pizza every day!
So, which city is better? New York is more exciting, and the museums are bigger. But Boston is quieter and friendlier, and it's easier to walk everywhere.
For a holiday, I prefer New York. For life, I prefer Boston. What about you?

sections.title: Grammar: comparatives

head: Adjective
Comparative
Rule
rows: vowel + consonant at the end: double it

rules: Use **than** after the comparative: *New York is bigger **than** Boston.*
**much** makes the difference bigger: *Amman is **much** warmer than Boston.*
examples: My sister is younger than me.
The subway is faster than the bus.
This coffee is more expensive than Sam's.

support.tr: Karşılaştırma (daha): kısa sıfatlar -er alır (cold → colder = daha soğuk), uzun sıfatların önüne more gelir (more expensive = daha pahalı). "-den/-dan" ekinin karşılığı than'dır ve sıfattan sonra gelir: New York is bigger than Boston = New York Boston'dan daha büyük. Türkçede önce "Boston'dan", sonra "daha büyük" gelir; İngilizcede önce bigger, sonra than Boston. Düzensizler: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther.
support.ar: المقارنة: الصفات القصيرة تأخذ ‎-er‎ (cold → colder = أبرد)، والصفات الطويلة نضع قبلها more (more expensive = أغلى). كلمة than تعني «من» في المقارنة: New York is bigger than Boston = نيويورك أكبر من بوسطن. الترتيب مثل العربية: الصفة ثم than ثم الشيء الثاني. العربية تستخدم وزن «أفعل» (أكبر، أبرد)، والإنجليزية ‎-er‎ أو more. الشاذة: good → better، bad → worse، far → farther.

tr.note: "daha" için more ve -er birlikte kullanılmaz; "-den" = than (from değil).
wrong: New York is more bigger than Boston.
right: New York is bigger than Boston.

ar.note: لا نجمع more مع ‎-er‎، و«من» في المقارنة هي than وليست from.
wrong: Amman is more warmer than Boston.
My city is more big than your city.
right: My city is bigger than your city.

sections.title: Write: Two places

model.heading: São Paulo and Boston — Lucas
text: São Paulo is much bigger than Boston. About twelve million people live there.
It's also hotter and noisier, and the traffic is worse.
Boston is cleaner and quieter, but the winter is much colder!
The food in São Paulo is better, of course.
But in Boston, my band plays every Friday at Sam's café.
São Paulo is more exciting, but for now, I prefer Boston.
